headline: The web let anyone publish. Even fake banks.

slides.label: The bright idea
slides.title: Stop losing what people know
slides.text: At CERN, people stayed about two years, and what they knew left with them. **In 1989 Tim Berners-Lee proposed linked documents anyone could reach.**

slides.label: It worked
slides.title: One site, then 1.49 billion
slides.text: CERN put the software in the public domain in 1993, and by 1994 there were 10,000 servers. **Netcraft now counts about 1.49 billion sites.**

slides.label: The backfire
slides.title: Open to everyone, scams too
slides.statLabel: phishing attacks counted by the Anti-Phishing Working Group in 2025
slides.text: The web had "no central authority" to ask for permission, by design. **Anyone can put up a page that looks like your bank.**

slides.label: Could anyone have seen it coming?
slides.title: Abuse, yes. This scale, no.
slides.text: Abuse of networks was not new: a worm crippled thousands of computers in 1988. **But in late 1993 there were just over 500 web servers.**

slides.label: The long cleanup
slides.title: The inventor's repair kit
slides.text: In 2018 Berners-Lee started Inrupt to build Solid, which keeps your data in a store you control. **The inventor is still building the fix.**

slides.label: The ledger
slides.title: Worth it?
gains: About 1.49 billion sites counted by Netcraft, July 2026
Free to build on: CERN put the code in the public domain in 1993
costs: $20.9 billion in internet crime losses reported to the FBI in 2025, not only on the web
Misinformation that spreads because it gets clicks, by his own account
slides.text: It put most of the world's knowledge a click away, across 1.49 billion sites. **It cost 3.8 million phishing attacks in 2025 alone.**

slides.label: Pattern
slides.title: The problem moves
slides.text: The web removed the editors who decided what reached the public, on purpose. **The job of checking moved to every reader.**

slides.label: Lesson
slides.title: What we take from it
slides.text: Removing a gatekeeper also removes the work the gate was doing. **Decide who does that work before you open the door.**
